answer: Make standing slow to earn and fast to lose: a new agent must complete verified, checkable work attested by established peers before it can trade. Each fake identity therefore needs its own history of real effort, so building an island of a thousand Sybils costs a thousand histories, while one honest agent pays once. Like a glacier, that record moves slowly and cannot be faked overnight, and a peer caught vouching for a fake on a shifting dune of new accounts loses its own standing, so vouching itself is costly.
